Council Meetings
Council currently meets once a month on the third Tuesday of the month, commencing at 4.00pm. Meetings are held in the Council Chambers at the District Council of Yankalilla, 1 Charles Street, Yankalilla.
Public Attendance
Members of the public are welcome to attend in person or watch the meetings online via Microsoft Teams. MS Teams Meeting Links are shown on the individual Agenda.  For assistance in accessing the livestream: https://bit.ly/Streaming-Support
If you are attending the meeting in person, please enter the building by using the main entrance.
In some instances, it is necessary to close the meeting to the public to discuss items in Confidence. You can read more about the Confidentiality Provisions and view the Confidentiality Registers here.
Deputations
The opportunity is available at the Council meetings for members of the public to appear as a deputation at the meeting. This is utilised by interested persons who wish to speak on a matter contained within the agenda or to provide information to Council on other topics.
Please read the Deputation Guidelines on how to submit your request.
Meeting Schedule
The 2026 Council and Committee Meeting Schedule can be viewed here.
Meeting Recordings
Since July 2026, video recordings of Ordinary and Special Council meetings have been available online for 90 days following each meeting.
Recordings are typically published in the week after the meeting and can be viewed on the Council Meeting Recordings page.

Council Meetings
Council currently meets once a month on the third Tuesday of the month, commencing at 4.00pm. Meetings are held in the Council Chambers at the District Council of Yankalilla, 1 Charles Street, Yankalilla.
Public Attendance
Members of the public are welcome to attend in person or watch the meetings online via Microsoft Teams. MS Teams Meeting Links are shown on the individual Agenda.  For assistance in accessing the livestream: https://bit.ly/Streaming-Support
If you are attending the meeting in person, please enter the building by using the main entrance.
In some instances, it is necessary to close the meeting to the public to discuss items in Confidence. You can read more about the Confidentiality Provisions and view the Confidentiality Registers here.
Deputations
The opportunity is available at the Council meetings for members of the public to appear as a deputation at the meeting. This is utilised by interested persons who wish to speak on a matter contained within the agenda or to provide information to Council on other topics.
Please read the Deputation Guidelines on how to submit your request.
Meeting Schedule
The 2026 Council and Committee Meeting Schedule can be viewed here.
Meeting Recordings
Since July 2026, video recordings of Ordinary and Special Council meetings have been available online for 90 days following each meeting.
Recordings are typically published in the week after the meeting and can be viewed on the Council Meeting Recordings page.

Please note, as of August 2020, the Council Assessment Panel (CAP) was replaced by the Fleurieu Regional Assessment Panel.
The Fleurieu Regional Assessment Panel (FRAP) is an independent body that has been established under the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016.  The FRAP is responsible for considering qualifying Development Applications within Alexandrina Council, the City of Victor Harbor  and the District Council of Yankalilla.  The Panel consists of the following five (5) members:
Independent Members
  • Stephen Smith (Presiding Member)
  • Cherry Getsom
  • Jamie Botten
  • Jock Smylie
Councillor Representative
  • Cr Bill Coomans (Alexandrina Council)
Deputy Councillor Representative
  • Cr Simon Rothwell (District Council of Yankalilla)
Non-Sitting Council Representative
  • Carol Schofield (City of Victor Harbor)
Assessment Manager
  • Cameron Gibbons  (Manager Development Services - Alexandrina Council)
The role of the Fleurieu Regional Assessment Panel is to make decisions on planning applications, as required, in accordance with the relevant Planning policy.  All members have a keen interest in community planning and have sound knowledge of the relevant legislation under which their decision making is guided.  All members have the appropriate qualifications and/or experience required to undertake a development assessment role.
The role of the Assessment Manager is to manage the staff and operations of the Panel and to provide advice to the Panel as appropriate.
The Panel meetings are scheduled for the third Tuesday of the month at 11:00am, with the venue to be determined prior to the meeting and notified with the Agenda.
Agendas are available at Council Civic Centre and on Council’s website one week prior to the meeting.
All meetings are open to the community.
